title: Microsoft 365 Copilot: users can upload local and OneDrive files to custom engine agents
summary: Hold: the billing exemption is stated for agents generally, but its cited licensing page covers only agents powered by the standard harness. Administrators must not assume that exemption covers every custom engine agent. The roadmap facts and documented access controls otherwise check out.

claims.claim: Block restricts access to the selected whole agent across the organisation.
claims.quote: These actions apply to the selected agent. ... Restrict access to an agent across the organization, preventing any user from using it.

claims.quote: However, blocking an agent that you created by using SharePoint or Microsoft Foundry only impacts its availability in Microsoft Copilot Chat.

claims.claim: Microsoft 365 admin center > Agents > Settings > User access reaches the agent and plugin access control.
claims.quote: Select Agents > Settings > User access to manage your organization's agents and plugins.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Why it matters; Risk assessment; Governance guidance; Governance controls
claims.claim: User access governs organisation-wide access to agents and plugins, rather than access to one selected agent.
claims.quote: Select who can access agents and plugins within your organization. ... Select Save to update your Copilot agent and plugin settings for your tenant.

claims.claim: All users is the default User access option.
claims.quote: All users - This option is the default. It means that all users in the organization can access agents and plugins, subject to the existing app policies and user assignments.

claims.claim: User access includes a No users option.
claims.quote: No users - This option means that no users in the organization can access agents and plugins.

claims.claim: User access includes an option to select specific users or groups.
claims.quote: Specific users or groups - This option lets you select specific users or groups in your organization to have access to agents and plugins.

claims.claim: POST https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/admin/configurationManagement/configurationMonitors can apply the documented User access baseline once.
claims.quote: POST https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/admin/configurationManagement/configurationMonitors ... applies a desired-state baseline once in applyOnce mode.
claims.fix: Keep the call. Add to controls[1].note: "The request body sets mode to applyOnce and baseline.resources to resourceType microsoft.agent.useraccess, resourceVersion 1, with properties.valueObject.userAssignmentCategory set to everyone or noOne." These details are already verified in the prose and at https://learn.microsoft.com/graph/utcm-agent-resources.

claims.claim: Setting mode to applyOnce applies the desired-state baseline once.
claims.quote: mode ... The possible values are: monitorOnly, applyOnce, unknownFutureValue. ... An active applyOnce monitor runs in the background on behalf of the signed-in administrator and then becomes inactive.

claims.claim: The User access baseline uses resourceType microsoft.agent.useraccess inside baseline.resources.
claims.quote: "displayName": "Agent user access", "resourceType": "microsoft.agent.useraccess"

claims.claim: The User access resource uses resourceVersion 1.
claims.quote: All resources on this page use resourceVersion: 1 and are singletons.

claims.claim: properties.valueObject.userAssignmentCategory accepts everyone or noOne to configure User access.
claims.quote: userAssignmentCategory ... Specifies whether all users or no users can access agents and plugins. ... everyone, noOne ... "properties": { "valueObject": { "userAssignmentCategory": "everyone" } }

claims.claim: Creating an applyOnce monitor requires the calling app's delegated ConfigurationMonitoring.ReadWrite.All permission.

claims.claim: For applyOnce on Agent resources the TCM service principal needs delegated CopilotPolicySettings.ReadWrite.
claims.quote: For remediation and applyOnce, grant it the CopilotPolicySettings.ReadWrite delegated permission.

claims.claim: AI Administrator is the required least-privileged signed-in user role for applyOnce on Agent resources.

claims.quote: Searched: useraccess resource text for specific-user/group properties and allowed values. Read Supported Agent resources and Supported resources for remediation and applyOnce in full; userAssignmentCategory lists only everyone and noOne.

claims.claim: The User access applyOnce automation is preview and beta, with production application use unsupported.
claims.quote: APIs under the /beta version in Microsoft Graph are subject to change. Use of these APIs in production applications is not supported.
